findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once, when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit value gets the same stale timestamp (process start time). The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued. It should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The test only checks that `queued` is not None, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: `to_dict` puts a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs
findings.body: `asdict(self)` returns `queued` as a `datetime`. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes this dict to `apply_async` as kwargs. With the JSON serializer the datetime may fail to serialize or may come back as a string. After the round trip, `from_dict` would build the dataclass with `queued` as a string, which is the wrong type. It is also possible that `from_dict` raises for unexpected types, since it only catches ValueError and TypeError. `queued` should be serialized explicitly, for example as an ISO string, and parsed back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: `where_should_sync` calls `should_sync` without `sync_source`
findings.body: The sync-cycle check is only applied in the outbound task. Other callers of `should_sync` ignore the source, which is fine for inbound. However, `sync_status_outbound` gained an `assignment_source` parameter in the abstract signature that no caller ever passes. This is dead plumbing and implies a status-cycle guard that does not exist.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg is passed to every integration's `sync_assignee_outbound`
findings.body: The task now always passes `assignment_source=...` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`. The abstract signature accepts `**kwargs`, but the diff does not update the concrete implementations. Any integration whose `sync_assignee_outbound` lacks `**kwargs` will raise a TypeError on every outbound sync, and the retry decorator will retry that error. Concrete implementations (Jira, VSTS, etc.) should be verified or updated.

findings.title: Cycle-prevention test covers only the assign path, not deassign or other-integration cases
findings.body: The only new test checks `assign` with a matching source. Missing cases: `deassign` with a source (which the inbound path uses), and the case where a different integration is the source and outbound sync must still happen. The `sync_group_assignee_inbound` tests also don't verify that an AssignmentSource is passed through.
